instructions: Cut the tofu crosswise into 8 slabs about 1/3 inch thick. Lay them on a plate lined with a clean towel, cover them with another towel and press gently. Leave them for 15 minutes.

Meanwhile, make the pickles. Peel the 2 carrots and a 4 inch piece of the daikon and cut them into thin matchsticks. In a bowl, stir 1/3 cup rice vinegar, 2 tbsp sugar and 1/2 tsp salt until the sugar dissolves. Add the vegetables and toss them. Leave them for at least 20 minutes, tossing once or twice.
Make the marinade. Peel the dry outer layers off the lemongrass and finely mince 1 1/2 tbsp of the pale lower part. Mince the 4 garlic cloves. Squeeze 2 tsp juice from the lime.

Pile the lemongrass and garlic on the board with 2 tsp sugar and 1/2 tsp salt. Mash them with the flat of your knife into a rough paste. Transfer it to a small bowl and stir in the lime juice, 1/2 tsp black pepper and 2 tbsp of the oil.
Stir 1 tbsp of the marinade into the 1/2 cup mayonnaise. Pat the tofu dry and brush the rest of the marinade over both sides of each slab.

Heat the last 2 tbsp of oil in a large nonstick skillet over medium-high heat for 1 minute. Add the tofu in a single layer and leave it alone for about 3 minutes, until the underside is golden and crisp at the edges. Stand back a little. It will spatter.
Flip the slabs and cook the other side for about 3 minutes, until it's golden. Transfer them to a rack or a plate lined with paper towels.
Meanwhile, cut the 2 cucumbers lengthwise into long thin strips. Pull a big handful of cilantro sprigs off the bunch. Drain the pickles well.

Put the baguettes straight on the oven rack for 5 minutes, until the crust is crisp and crackly. Split each one along the top, leaving the bottom joined, and spread 2 tbsp of the lemongrass mayonnaise inside.
Lay 2 tofu slabs in each roll, then add the cucumber, a good stuffing of pickles and the cilantro. If you're packing them for lunch, wrap each one tightly in parchment.
Serve with the sriracha on the side.
method_notes: No tofu banh mi read had 20 or more ratings, and RecipeTin Eats, the trusted cook for Vietnamese, has no tofu version, so this follows Andrea Nguyen's Viet World Kitchen recipe. All the versions press firm tofu, season it with lemongrass, garlic and something salty, fry it until golden and build the sandwich with mayonnaise, pickled carrot and daikon, cucumber and cilantro. The lead pounds lemongrass, garlic, sriracha, lime, sugar, salt and pepper into a paste and stirs some of it into the mayonnaise; Great British Chefs marinates for hours with fish sauce, and Live Eat Learn uses soy and sesame oil. Here the paste is mashed by hand instead of in a mini processor, the sriracha moves out of the marinade to the side, and the quick pickle follows Great British Chefs.
